analysis.one_liner: Siemens Ltd makes industrial automation, digital-industries and smart-infrastructure (building/electrical) equipment and rail mobility systems in India, after spinning off its power/energy equipment business as a separately listed Siemens Energy India in April 2025.
tags: Raw -22% drawdown is a demerger illusion
analysis.whats_happening: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) results on 11 Aug 2026 showed revenue up 14.8% YoY to ₹4,714 cr and order backlog up 9.6% to ₹46,670 cr, but the headlined ₹2,143 cr net profit (+407% YoY) was almost entirely a one-off ₹2,099 cr gain on selling the Low Voltage Motors business - profit from continuing operations actually fell to ₹343 cr from ₹422 cr as EBITDA margin contracted ~340bps to 9.15% on costlier commodities and a weaker rupee. Separately, NCLT approved folding the Rail Automation subsidiary into Siemens Ltd (Sept 2026) and the company took full ownership of C&S Electric (25 Sep 2026). The next quarterly result (Q2 FY27, Jul-Sep 2026) has no confirmed date yet - Not verified, typically due by mid-November under SEBI's 45-day rule.
analysis.plain_terms: Siemens supplies the machines and systems that run factories, buildings and railways in India. In April 2025 it split off its power-equipment business into a separate listed company, Siemens Energy India, so comparing today's numbers to pre-2025 history without adding that back is misleading. The latest quarter's eye-catching 400%+ profit jump is not the business suddenly getting better - it is a one-time gain from selling a motors factory, and the underlying, recurring profit actually went down. The real tension: orders and revenue keep growing, but the profit margin on each order is shrinking because raw materials (copper, steel) and the weaker rupee cost more.
analysis.quarters: Revenue has grown steadily (+14.6-14.8% YoY in the last two reported quarters) and the order backlog keeps climbing (₹45,033 cr in Mar-26, ₹46,670 cr in Jun-26). But the FY ended March 2026 was an unusual 18-month transition period (Oct 2024-Mar 2026) as Siemens AG globally shifted its reporting calendar, so quarter-over-quarter comparisons straddling that change are not strictly comparable. Reported net profit swung wildly - ₹485 cr (Sep-25) → ₹278 cr (Dec-25) → ₹370 cr (Mar-26) → ₹2,143 cr (Jun-26) - but that last spike is the LVM sale gain; on continuing operations, profit actually slipped from ₹422 cr to ₹343 cr YoY as EBITDA margin fell from roughly 11% toward 9%.
analysis.performance_read: Raw price data shows the stock down 22% from its October 2024 peak of ₹4,648.66 to ₹3,624 now - but this overstates the fall for a specific reason: that peak was set before the April 2025 1:1 demerger of Siemens Energy India (SEIL). Every Siemens Ltd holder since then also owns one SEIL share per share, and SEIL closed 16 Oct 2026 at ₹2,889. Add the two together (₹3,624 + ₹2,889 = ₹6,513) and shareholders are actually about 40% above the 2024 peak, not 22% below it. The same distortion understates the quoted 3-year (+73.97%) and 5-year (+179.08%) returns, which track only the post-split Siemens Ltd price; reconstructing the pre-demerger base from those figures and adding back today's SEIL value gives an approximate demerger-adjusted return of roughly +210% over 3 years and +400% over 5 years (estimate, not an official combined-index figure) - comfortably ahead of the Nifty (+16.83%/+25.27%) and even peer ABB India's raw 5-year return (+284.63%). The 1-year figure needs no adjustment (both endpoints are post-demerger): stock +16.76% vs Nifty -9.53%, though behind ABB's +32.56%. Over 3 months the stock held up better than both (-0.46% vs Nifty -4.88% and ABB -8.33%).
analysis.valuation_read: Sources disagree sharply on the P/E - screener.in's live figure shows 85.8x while some aggregators show roughly 39x - and the gap traces back to the one-off ₹2,099 cr LVM sale gain: including it in trailing profit inflates EPS and drops the P/E to ~39x, while stripping it out (closer to recurring earnings) pushes it to ~85x. Why it looks cheap on one measure: a one-time asset sale temporarily flattered trailing earnings, not better ongoing profitability. Whether it's actually cheap: on the recurring-earnings basis, plus a P/B of ~9.3x against ROE of ~19%, Siemens trades at a rich premium typical of India-listed MNC capital-goods franchises, priced for the order book converting into margin recovery rather than for today's compressed quarterly profitability.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is clearly volume-led, not margin-led: revenue is up 14.6-14.8% YoY and the order backlog is up 9.3-9.6% YoY to ₹46,670 cr (about 2.5 years of revenue cover), driven broadly across Digital Industries (+25%), Mobility (+13%) and Smart Infrastructure (+11%). But EBITDA margin has moved the wrong way, contracting roughly 340bps to ~9.15% as commodity costs and rupee depreciation eat into each order's profitability - more business is coming in, but each rupee of it is earning less than before.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet risk is minimal - borrowings of just ₹307 cr against reserves of ₹13,769 cr, effectively debt-free. The real risk here is business/margin risk, not financial risk: rising commodity costs and currency depreciation are compressing operating margins even as order volumes grow. Whether reported profit is actually converting into operating cash flow is Not verified - check the cash flow statement on Screener for the OCF/PAT conversion ratio before assuming the headline profit (especially the LVM one-off, which is a book gain on a business sale, not a recurring cash inflow) reflects usable cash.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter is Siemens AG, held through Siemens International Holding B.V. (53.7%) and other group entities, totalling 75% - unchanged for over a year. Promoter pledge has been reduced to 0% as of June 2026, down from 6.67% in March 2025, a clear de-risking signal. No marquee individual or activist Indian investor appears on the register based on available data - this is an institution/promoter-dominated stock, not one with a well-known retail investor backing it.
strengths: Order backlog of ₹46,670 cr, up 9.6% YoY, giving roughly 2.5 years of revenue visibility
Effectively debt-free: borrowings of ₹307 cr against reserves of ₹13,769 cr
Promoter pledge cut to 0% in June 2026 from 6.67% a year earlier
Broad-based revenue growth of 14.8% YoY across Digital Industries (+25%), Mobility (+13%) and Smart Infrastructure (+11%)
watchpoints: EBITDA margin down ~340bps YoY to ~9.15% in the latest quarter on commodity cost and rupee pressure
Headline net profit growth (+407% YoY) is almost entirely a one-off ₹2,099 cr gain from the LVM business sale; continuing-operations profit actually fell to ₹343 cr from ₹422 cr
Stock has lagged peer ABB India over 1 year (+16.76% vs +32.56%) and on an unadjusted basis over 5 years
Valuation is rich on a recurring-earnings basis (~85x P/E, ~9.3x P/B), leaving little room for margin disappointment
analysis.one_thing: Whether EBITDA margin recovers toward the ~11% levels seen before FY26 in the next one or two quarters - that single number will show whether the order-book growth is translating into real, sustainable profit or is being eaten up by commodity and currency costs.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly P&L, order book and segment data cross-checked across screener.in, Business Standard, MarketScreener and Kotak Neo. P/E (85.8x vs ~39x) and ROE (19.2% vs 15.64%) figures conflict across sources depending on whether the one-off LVM divestment gain is included in trailing earnings - used screener.in's live fetch as the primary figure. Demerger-adjusted long-term return figures (3Y/5Y) are an approximation reconstructed from the supplied headline returns plus today's Siemens Energy India price, not an official combined-index calculation. Operating cash flow conversion was not verified - check Screener's cash flow statement directly.
